east_texas.headline: A gray, breezy start, then the coldest stretch of the season so far through Thanksgiving.
east_texas.summary: Low clouds behind Sunday's front are slow to clear, so the morning stays gray with a north wind near 10 mph. Some sun returns this afternoon with a high in the upper 50s. Tonight turns colder, in the upper 30s. A fast-moving system may bring a few light showers late Tuesday night, mainly south and east of Tyler. Lows drop to near freezing Wednesday through Friday mornings, colder in rural low spots.
east_texas.rain_note: Dry today and tonight. About a 20% chance of light rain late Tuesday night into early Wednesday.

days.text: Mostly sunny and chilly. Slight chance of light rain after midnight.
Sunny. Lows near freezing, upper 20s in rural cold spots.
Sunny and cool after a cold start.
Mostly sunny after another cold morning.
Warmer with south winds, highs back in the 60s and 70s.

facts.p: No severe risk through Tuesday night
No notable outages in Smith or nearby counties
NWS lows 32–34; rural cold spots in the upper 20s

panels.title: Cold mornings, sunny afternoons
paras: NWS Shreveport says a second, stronger disturbance dives through Tuesday night with patchy light rain, mainly over southern and eastern areas. It then reinforces the cold air, with much of the region near or below freezing Wednesday through Friday mornings.
Thanksgiving Day looks dry and sunny with highs in the upper 50s. Temperatures return to near normal this weekend as south winds come back.

panels.title: Warmer and wetter into early December
paras: The Climate Prediction Center favors above-normal temperatures and above-normal rain for Texas from Nov 29 to Dec 5, with low confidence. Weather models show highs in the 70s around Dec 1 and a chance of rain near Dec 3.
El Niño remains strong to very strong. It tends to favor an active southern storm track this winter.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NWS Fort Worth, NOAA Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Weather Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, Texas A&M Forest Service, PowerOutage.us, KLTV closings.

nm.headline: Snow showers move through the northern mountains this afternoon into early Tuesday, then a long dry stretch.
nm.summary: A fast-moving trough brings rain and snow showers to northern New Mexico starting late this morning. NWS Albuquerque expects a brief burst of heavy snow in the mountains this afternoon, favoring west and southwest slopes of the Sangre de Cristos, with up to about 6 inches on the peaks. Below 8,000 feet expect a rain and snow mix with a dusting or less. Las Vegas could see its first flakes of the season. Dry, tranquil weather returns Tuesday and lasts through the weekend.

days.text: Rain and snow showers develop late morning, heaviest in the afternoon. Snow showers linger in the east tonight.
Sunny and cold. Very cold night in the high valleys.
Mostly sunny and milder. Light winds.
Dry northwest flow. A more active pattern may begin in early December.

nm.snow_note: Readings from the start of today, before this afternoon's snow. Taos Powderhorn is at 138% of median and Gallegos Peak at 106%.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu reports 6 inches of new snow in the last 48 hours. Resort base depths include man-made snow. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: A quick round of mountain snow
paras: NWS Albuquerque says the strongest lift reaches north-central New Mexico early this afternoon, with a brief period of heavy snow in the mountains. West and southwest slopes of the Sangre de Cristos are favored, with localized amounts up to about 6 inches on the peaks.
Between 6,000 and 8,000 feet it will be a rain and snow mix. Snow levels run lower on the east side, where Las Vegas and Santa Rosa could see flakes but no more than an inch.

panels.title: Slick spots on US-64 and NM-38
paras: NMRoads lists US-64 from east of Taos to west of Eagle Nest and NM-38 from Questa to Red River as snow packed and icy. NM-518, NM-434 and the interstates had no reported issues early this morning.
Expect slick travel above 8,000 feet this afternoon into Tuesday morning. Check nmroads.com before heading out.

panels.title: Dry week, then a more active pattern
paras: A ridge builds Tuesday and Wednesday, keeping winds light and nights very cold in the high valleys. Dry northwest flow continues through Saturday.

NWS Albuquerque says a stronger Pacific jet may bring a more active storm track in the first week of December, though warmer air with it would mean high snow levels. El Niño remains strong to very strong.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, OnTheSnow, Sipapu snow report, NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
